title: Ordinary-cut lemma reuse parent saturation
paper_question: can acquisition/retention/selection that prices future verification and revision improve later cognition beyond equally adaptive program-library parents?

entries.citation: Mooney, The Effect of Rule Use on the Utility of Explanation-Based Learning, IJCAI-89, pp. 725-730
entries.what_parent_explained: Utility depends on how learned Horn macros are used. Full-use chaining with domain rules degrades performance; limited-use (fire only if the learned rule completely solves the current goal; no backchaining on antecedents) improves it. Search strategy changes the sign. 1-step conclusion matching is the limited-use extreme.
entries.adopt: Limited-use as the first later-search policy; do not chain unrestricted macros.
entries.adapt: Map limited-use onto 2-decision native search rather than 1-step alias.
entries.reject: Reading SCREENED_NEGATIVE_IN_DOMAIN as no useful cut.
entries.leave_open: Whether limited 2-step use of the 22 pays after match cost.
entries.prior_information_added: IJCAI-89 full text; Principia/blocks-world full-vs-limited tables; NP-complete match warning.
entries.remaining_question: Does limited 2-step use of the 22 have positive utility, or is even that negative?

entries.citation: Minton, Quantitative results concerning the utility of explanation-based learning, Artificial Intelligence 42(2-3):363-391, 1990
entries.source_type_note: AIJ 1990 closed (Unpaywall/OpenAlex/S2 no OA PDF; ScienceDirect 403). Formula from Langley 2023 slides quoting Minton 1990 and Marks 1991 quoting Minton 1988a/b. AAAI-88 CDN served bundled proceedings, not an isolated extract.
entries.what_parent_explained: A rule is useful only if cumulative savings times applicability frequency exceed match cost. Estimate from the producing example, validate empirically, discard negative utility. This is the quantitative utility problem.
entries.adopt: Exact formula as retention test for the 22 lemmas.
entries.adapt: Native units: decision-count / action-attempts / compile cost; do not add incommensurable dimensions.
entries.leave_open: Training-only estimate that predicts held-out utility without protected-task peeking.
entries.prior_information_added: Closed-access status; formula quotation trail; 1-step ApplicFreq~0 implies Utility~-AvrMatchCost.
entries.remaining_question: After refactoring+2-decision, is any lemma's training-estimated utility positive?
